transcript.content: hey, I'm Berry. tell me your dream however it comes back to you, even just a scrap of it.
it started snowing inside the office. big slow flakes from the ceiling lights.

snow inside, from the lights… that's the kind of thing that makes a place feel wrong in the best way.

what happened next?
nobody else looked up, everyone just kept typing. it felt really quiet and peaceful.

everyone just kept typing, like it was the most normal thing in the world.

were you the only one who felt like looking up?
yeah, I was the only one. it all felt soft and watery, like the colours were running into each other.

it sounds lovely, actually. soft around the edges, and you were in it but also a little apart.

did you do anything, or just watch for a bit?
I just watched for a bit. the snow built up on the desks and keyboards and carpet till everything was white. only the tops of the computer screens showed.

everything going white while no one even notices… it's a strange sort of hush.

and then what, if you remember?
Dele came over. my manager. he's a tall man in a blue suit. he walked over to tell me something.

after all that quiet, someone finally coming over to you…

did the snow seem to bother him at all?
no, it didn't seem to bother him. and while he was talking he turned into a snowman, still in the blue suit, still holding his coffee mug.

he just kept being Dele, blue suit and coffee, but made of snow

that's a wild thing to see mid-conversation, did he seem aware of it at all?
he didn't seem aware, or I don't remember. it wasn't scary, it felt peaceful.

there's something nice about that. not everything turning strange has to be frightening.

how did it end? or what's the last thing you remember?
I made a snowball and it glowed a little in my hand, and then I woke up.

a glowing snowball, just before waking… that feels like the kind of thing that follows you into the day.

if you could pause the dream on one moment, the one frame you'd keep — what would you be looking at?
Dele as a snowman in his blue suit, holding the mug. the whole office white around him.

it's a perfect picture, him half office half snow, all that white around him.

and did it feel like the dream was saying something to you, or was it just… a moment that stayed?
just a moment that stayed, I think. I don't know if it meant anything. it just felt right.

that's enough, I think. a moment that felt right.

the mug, the snowball, the computer screens… or did nothing in particular stand out?
the snowball glowing in my hand stood out most. and the snow still falling.

so it started snowing inside your office, big slow flakes falling from the ceiling lights, and no one else looked up. the place went soft and watery, colours running together, and you just watched as the snow piled up on desks and keyboards until everything was white except the tops of the screens. then your manager Dele walked over, tall in his blue suit, and mid-conversation he turned into a snowman, still holding his coffee mug, still not bothered by any of it. it felt peaceful the whole time, and in the end you made a snowball that glowed in your hand, right before you woke up.

did I get that right, or is there anything I missed?
yeah that's right, you got it. it all felt peaceful, even the strange bits.

even the strange bits kept that quiet. that's what makes it stay with you, I think.

would you like me to draw it for you?
yes, I'd like that.

let's make it into a picture then.

there are a few ways it could be drawn. soft watercolour washes, where the whole scene melts softly like a memory of snow. muted pastel drawing, like a hush made visible, every surface of the same quiet powder. delicate ink line and wash, fragile and hand-drawn, every line calm. or just as it looked in the dream, soft and white, real but not quite. which of those feels closest, or would you describe it your own way?
soft and white, real but not quite. that feels closest.

soft and white, real but not quite. I like that. I'll start with you.

and since you're in it, I'll draw you too. would you like to be drawn as you are — you can tell me a bit about yourself — or however I imagine you?
however you imagine me is fine, I don't mind.

I'll draw you however I imagine you, then.

I'm sketching you and Dele and the office and the coffee mug now. everything is being sketched and will appear on the right over the next minute or two. once it's there, if anything looks off, just say.
it looks right, I can't see anything wrong.
does it look the way you remember it?
yeah, it looks right. it's calm, like how it felt.

that's good, it feels calm like you remember.

I'll draw the moments of the dream in order now, each one carrying on from the ones before it. they'll appear on the right as they're ready.
okay, I'll wait.

the first moment is up now, snow starting to fall inside the office, big slow flakes.

does it look the way you remember it?
yeah, that's right. slow flakes from the lights, no one looking up.

the quiet of it comes through, everyone just going on with their day as the snow arrives.

the next moments are being drawn. they'll appear on the right as they're ready, and I'll tell you each time.
okay, waiting.

the second moment is up now, of you watching the others keep typing as the snow falls.

does it look the way you remember it?
yeah, it does. it had that same soft feel, them not noticing at all.
glad it matches. I'll keep drawing the next moments and tell you as each one is ready.
okay.

the third moment is up now, snow building up on desks, keyboards, and carpet until everything's white.

does it look the way you remember it?
yeah, it does. all white with just the tops of the screens showing.
that's the third one down. i'm glad it stays true to what you saw. the next ones are still being drawn and will show up on the right soon.
okay, no rush.
the fourth moment is up now, Dele walking over in his blue suit. does it look the way you remember it?
yeah, that's him. tall, in the blue suit, coming over like he was about to say something.
that's the fourth one down, and it sounds like it's right. the last two moments are still being drawn and I'll let you know when they're up.
okay.
the fifth moment is up now, of Dele turning into a snowman while talking, still in his blue suit and holding his coffee mug. does it look the way you remember it?
yeah, it does. still him, just snow. he's still got the mug and the blue suit.

that's five. good.

one more moment left, the snowball glowing in your hand. it's being drawn now and should be up soon.
okay.
the last moment is up now, the snowball glowing in your hand. does it look the way you remember it?
yeah, that's it. a little glow in your hand, right before I woke up. feels about right.
I'm glad it feels right. Your dream is all drawn now, six pictures on the right in order. Thank you for sharing it with me, you can look through it any time.
